title: Apprenticeship Funding
subtitle: Fund the classroom block without budgeting from a grant that closed last year

blocks.text: An apprentice learns to measure twice and cut once. Funding deserves the same courtesy, especially when an old web page is still cheerfully offering a grant that has closed.

Provinces and territories run apprenticeships. Your funding can mix wages, Employment Insurance during approved school training, the interest-free Canada Apprentice Loan, provincial help, employer or union support and tax breaks. The right mix depends on your trade, your registration, your training block and where you live.
The federal Apprenticeship Incentive Grant and Apprenticeship Completion Grant closed on March 31, 2025. They are not open for 2026.

items.title: “Every Red Seal apprentice still receives federal progress and completion grants.”
items.text: Those grants closed in 2025. Help today comes through other routes. An archived success story cannot pay for Tuesday’s tools.

blocks.text: Canada: Apprenticeship grants status
Knowing which funding is open today lets you plan your school block without counting on money that is gone.
blocks.detail: Your wages, EI, a loan and local help each arrive on a different timeline.
blocks.extra: Section 02 shows who holds your apprenticeship file.

sections.title: Your Province or Territory Holds Your Apprenticeship File

blocks.text: Confirm your trade, registration number, employer or sponsor, your hours so far, your training level and your school dates with your provincial or territorial apprenticeship office. Not every listed trade is a Red Seal trade, and the rules for signing up vary.

items.title: WAGES
items.text: Paid training on the job is still the base. Ask how your wage changes at each level and what stops while you are in class.

items.title: EI FOR APPRENTICES
items.text: Apprentices in approved full-time school training may get EI. Get the 16-digit referral code from your apprenticeship office or school.

items.title: CANADA APPRENTICE LOAN
items.text: Red Seal apprentices who qualify can ask for up to $4,000, interest-free, for each block of school training, up to $20,000 over a lifetime.

items.title: LOCAL AND WORKPLACE HELP
items.text: Check tuition, travel, childcare, tools, living allowances, union funds, employer top-ups and tax breaks one by one.

blocks.text: Provinces and territories control apprenticeship sign-up and certificates. The Red Seal Program sets standards across provinces. It does not replace your local office.
The Canada Apprentice Loan can pay for tuition, tools, equipment, living costs, lost wages or family needs during school training.

items.title: “A Canada Apprentice Loan is a grant because it is interest-free.”
items.text: It is borrowed money. Having no interest is a useful feature, not a ceremonial cancellation of repayment.

blocks.text: Canada: Canada Apprentice Loan

sections.title: Cover the Gap Between Your Last Paycheque and Your First Benefit

blocks.text: Before training starts, confirm four things in writing, not from memory.

items.title: Registration
items.text: Your apprenticeship office shows you as a registered apprentice, at the right level, for this block.

items.title: Record of Employment
items.text: Your employer will issue an ROE with Code J, the reason used when an apprentice leaves for school training.

items.title: School dates
items.text: Your class start and end dates, and the date tuition is due.

items.title: Final pay
items.text: The date and amount of your last paycheque before class, so you know how long you must cover on your own.

blocks.text: Apply for EI and give your 16-digit referral code. If you do not have the code, contact your apprenticeship office or school and give it to Service Canada as soon as you can.

You can ask for the Canada Apprentice Loan up to three months before school training starts, and if approved, it can arrive on your first day. It can bridge the timing gap. Borrow it against a written budget, not as an automatic $4,000 tool-shopping festival.
The federal government announced a new Apprenticeship Training Grant for 2026–27. Check that it is officially open, and who qualifies, before you add any money from it to your budget.

items.title: “EI begins automatically when the employer issues the ROE.”
items.text: You must apply, give your referral details and send your reports. The ROE is evidence, not a small electronic application elf.

blocks.text: Key takeaway: plan apprenticeship funding one training block at a time. Check which programs are open, get your referral code, apply for EI and loans on time, and budget for the timing gap without counting on closed or just-announced funding.
Meet Owen
paragraphs: Owen MacLeod is an electrical apprentice in Halifax. His second school block starts in eight weeks. His goal is to get through it without falling behind on rent.
He builds his budget around a $1,000 federal grant. His cousin got the same grant in 2024. Owen adds it to his plan, along with his last paycheque and some savings.

Then he goes to apply. The page says the grant closed on March 31, 2025. It had retired, apparently without updating the family group chat. His budget now has a $1,000 hole, and tuition is due in three weeks.
His first idea is to take the full $4,000 Canada Apprentice Loan and figure it out later. A new drill set is calling his name. Then he decides to map the gap first and borrow only what the map says.
He confirms his school dates with his apprenticeship office and gets his 16-digit referral code. He asks his boss to issue his ROE with Code J, and he applies for EI the week class starts.
The twist is in the dates. His EI will not arrive until three weeks into class, and his last paycheque comes before the first day. That three-week stretch is the real gap.

Owen borrows $2,300 to cover tuition and those three weeks. He walks into class without the old grant and without a surprise. His plan is less nostalgic and considerably more solvent. The drill set can wait for his next raise.

blocks.text: Search results often show apprenticeship grants that have closed. Read the status note and the page date before you count on any amount or deadline.
What resolved the conflict?
A grant that closed in 2025 cannot pay for a 2026 training block. Check that a program is open, then build your plan from the routes still available.
Owen covered his school block by borrowing $2,300 for the real gap instead of the full $4,000.
blocks.detail: Mapping when each payment arrives keeps your own loan small and your rent paid.
blocks.extra: The quick check in Section 05 tests whether you can spot the next move.

sections.title: Quick Check: Choose the Best Next Move

items.title: Who runs apprenticeship sign-up and certificates?
items.detail: Your province or territory, through its apprenticeship office.

items.title: Which two old federal grants are closed?
items.detail: The Apprenticeship Incentive Grant and the Apprenticeship Completion Grant closed on March 31, 2025.

items.title: What is the Canada Apprentice Loan limit for each training block?
items.detail: Up to $4,000 interest-free for each block of school training, up to $20,000 over a lifetime.

items.title: Why does the 16-digit code matter?
items.detail: It is the referral code Service Canada needs to process your EI claim for approved school training.

items.title: What should you check before you budget a newly announced program?
items.detail: That it is officially open and who qualifies. An announced program is not yet money you can count on.

sections.title: Your Action (Fill Out Form): Apprenticeship Training-Block Funding Map

blocks.text: Use short labels, not apprenticeship, EI, loan or bank numbers. Keep private details in the official websites.

Keep proof that you finished each school block. It helps you move up a level and supports employer records, provincial funding, your future certificate and any program that asks for proof. Mark every source OPEN, APPLIED, APPROVED or CLOSED. “I heard about it” is not a cash-flow category.

items.title: Registered apprentice
items.text: A person officially signed up with a provincial or territorial apprenticeship office.

items.title: Technical training
items.text: The approved classroom part of an apprenticeship.

items.title: Referral code
items.text: A 16-digit code that proves your school training is approved, for EI.

items.title: Code J
items.text: The ROE reason used when an apprentice leaves work for school training.

items.title: Canada Apprentice Loan
items.text: An interest-free federal loan for approved school training blocks.

items.title: Red Seal
items.text: A standard and certificate for certain trades that is recognized across provinces.

items.title: Journeyperson
items.text: A person certified to work in a trade under local rules.

quiz.question: True or False: “Every Red Seal apprentice still receives federal progress and completion grants.”

questions: Which province or territory and trade are you in, and are you a registered apprentice? (Yes / No / Not sure)
When does your next school block start and end, and when is tuition due?
Do you have your 16-digit referral code for EI? (Yes / Not yet / Not sure)
When will your last paycheque arrive before class, and about how much will it be?
About how much will tuition, tools and living costs be during the block? An estimate is fine.
Which funding will you apply for, and when? List each one.
